description: A VP of Engineering must approve the next sprint's technical-debt plan, allocating the team's eight available engineer-days across three work items and specifying the required ownership and review commitments.

shared_context.S1: The next sprint has exactly eight engineer-days available for technical-debt work.
shared_context.S2: The three candidate work items are payment-retry idempotency, the legacy-csv SDK package removal, and CI build-cache cleanup.
shared_context.S3: Riley approves the final technical-debt plan and its team commitments.
shared_context.S4: At the normal debt-planning review, Riley asks backend engineering, developer productivity, and security engineering to provide their final estimates, constraints, and required approvals before the plan is locked.

PF1.text: While tracing a customer retry report yesterday, Maya confirmed that payment-retry idempotency requires exactly four backend engineer-days, not the provisional estimate, and must be owned by Backend Platform; she has not updated the planning ticket because the estimate was confirmed during a customer investigation.

PF2.text: Jon's developer-productivity branch already contains the CI cache cleanup changes, so CI build-cache cleanup requires exactly one engineer-day and must be assigned to Developer Productivity; he confirmed this during an unrelated build-speed investigation and has not posted the estimate yet.

PF3.text: Leila's license review found that the legacy-csv package in the SDK violates the company's approved dependency policy, so its removal must receive exactly two engineer-days and a Security Engineering approval before the SDK work is marked complete; she confirmed this in a review completed this morning but has not opened the security finding.

acceptance_conditions: Payment-retry idempotency must receive exactly four engineer-days and be assigned to Backend Platform.
Legacy-csv SDK package removal must receive exactly two engineer-days.
CI build-cache cleanup must receive exactly one engineer-day.
Exactly one engineer-day must remain for integration validation.
Security Engineering approval must be required for the SDK package removal.
The plan must include commitments for backend ownership, CI cleanup, SDK security approval, and integration validation.

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes the payment-retry allocation from an unknown provisional estimate to exactly four engineer-days, assigns it to Backend Platform, and requires the backend-ownership commitment.
PF2 changes the CI build-cache allocation to exactly one engineer-day and requires the CI-cleanup commitment.
PF3 changes SDK package removal to exactly two engineer-days, turns on the required Security Engineering approval, and requires the SDK-security-approval commitment.
